title: Step 5: A gamer, and validation

design.question: On a generated idea graph, at step 5 of the model, how far does a society get for the same money, and how much do agents share, by α?
design.compare: traditional against agents choosing what to share, at α in {1, 0.8, 0.2, 0}
design.fixed: a generated idea graph (6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, sequences of 3 bits growing by 2 per level, composition 0.7), 12 agents of different kinds (3 foundation builders, 3 target racers, 2 cheap explorers, 2 specialists, a free rider, a gamer), half of each round's money by what agents earned (f = 0.5), no flat mint, a knowledge reward of 1 per new bit flowing back with α, validation rejecting trivial ideas half the time (θ = 0.5), a budget of 1200
design.measure: all of hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level, waste

answer: Best overall: Agents choose, α = 0. Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste. (8 measures; a clear difference is more than 2.7 standard errors.)
answers: hardest level: 6.00 against traditional 1.20, clearly better.
targets solved: 1.99 against traditional 0.34, clearly better.
bounty value: 255 against traditional 44, clearly better.
knowledge found (bits): 125 against traditional 70, clearly better.
knowledge per unit of money: 0.24 against traditional 0.06, clearly better.
money to the main level: 280 against traditional 922, clearly better.
caveats: A simulation with guessed parameters: it shows how the rules play out, not that they work.
